grade.first_issue: The decisive induction step is invalid: W_{n,p} is defined from an arbitrary subcollection of the original prime-support sets and is not associated with any sequence satisfying the same greedy rule with an initial term having k-1 prime factors. Thus the inductive hypothesis cannot be applied. This leaves eventual stabilization of V_n—the central structural claim—unproved, so Rule E caps the score at 3.
grade.summary: The hitting-set reformulation and the conditional argument that a stabilized finite union of divisibility classes has a translation period are sound. However, the proof of stabilization is precisely the hard part of the problem, and the submitted induction does not establish it. Repairing this requires a new structural finiteness argument rather than a routine correction.
strengths: Correctly reformulates the gcd conditions using hitting sets and divisibility by squarefree products.
Correctly observes that if V_n eventually stabilized, the stabilized set would be periodic modulo the lcm of finitely many generators.
The proposed backward-extension idea can be repaired using V_N⊆V_j and the greedy minimality of a_{j+1}.

errors.description: The inductive hypothesis applies only to V-sets arising from sequences generated by the same greedy rule. No such sequence is constructed for W_{n,p}; merely having S_1\{p} as a hitting set does not imply stabilization. Indeed, arbitrary families all hit by a fixed finite set can have nonstabilizing finite-prefix hitting sets.

The assertion that every inclusion-minimal hitting set has size at most |S_1| is false in general. For example, with S_1={p,q} and further sets {q,r_i}, the set {p,r_1,…,r_m} is an inclusion-minimal hitting set larger than S_1. This claim is not essential to the later argument.

The statement that the sequence agrees with the increasing enumeration of V_N all the way back to a_1 is justified only by saying 'by induction.' The displayed equality V_N=V_{N-1} alone cannot be iterated backward; one must instead use V_N⊆V_j and greediness to exclude an element of V_N between a_j and a_{j+1}.
